newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rank shares dive on trading update.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rank shares dive on trading update.

text.p: More than 300 million pounds ($490 million) was wiped off the value of British leisure company Rank Group Plc on Friday following a disappointing trading statement.

Rank, owner of the Hard Rock cafes, also announced a definitive agreement to sell its remaining 20 percent stake in office equipment joint venture Ranx Xerox to Xerox Corp of the U.S. in a deal worth as much as one billion pounds.
Rank said the disposal would have a broadly neutral effect on its earnings this year.
But share prices fell almost 10 percent and analysts cut forecasts after Rank said underlying turnover grew only one percent in the five months to the end of May.
"In the first half they will do well to match what they did last year although we should see an improvement in the second half," said analyst Greg Feehely of Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.

He said he was cutting his 1997 profit forecast by 10 million pounds to 335 million pounds, following the weakness in the first half. Rank had pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit of 297 million pounds in 1996.
Rank shares, which have underperformed the market by over 20 percent in the past year, shed 40p to 385.5p by 1145 GMT.

Rank said operating profit from continuing businesses rose seven percent in the first five months of 1997. Higher profit from Hard Rock, Holiday and Leisure divisions was offset by lower results from Film and Entertainment Services.
The real problem area was U.S. video duplication, where volumes fell 25 percent as a result of the timing of releases.

Feehely said the timing and structure of payments in the Rank Xerox deal were not particularly attractive. But he saw margin for a modest recovery in the share price as bargain hunters entered the market.

Rank, exiting the Rank Xerox venture it joined in 1956, will receive a 500 million pound initial instalment, two further payments of 220 million plus a possible 60 million pounds dependent on performance.
The disposal is the latest in a 1.3 billion pound series of sales since Rank chief executive Andrew Teare joined the company in April 1996.

Rank plans to use the proceeds from the Xerox sale to repurchase up to 250 million pounds of its own shares. The remainder will be used to cut debt or will be invested in the group's core leisure operations.

Rank is expanding its leisure business aggressively, planning to pump some 1.5 billion pounds into UK sites over the next five years. It also plans to open more than 30 Hard Rock sites around the globe between now and the turn of the century. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
